plans.name: Usage account
plans.note: Account quotas and stock availability must be checked before deploying 50 concurrent machines; no quota approval implied.

knobs.label: Data-center location
knobs.why: The public plans API lists location_cost overrides only for 'sao', at 1.5x monthly and hourly on 54 vc2/vhp/vhf/voc plans (e.g. vc2-4c-8gb $40 -> $60).

caveats: DIY infrastructure rather than an agent-managed sandbox: guest installation, HTTPS/domain setup, abuse controls and operations are customer responsibilities. Linux guest administrative capabilities are not preinstalled agent features. 30% guest CPU utilization does not reduce allocated-compute charges. Unknowns remain null; a partial subtotal is not a complete invoice.

Hourly price discrepancy: vultr.com/pricing (Wayback 2026-09-26) and the billing doc imply hour = monthly/672 with a 672 h cap ($40/mo -> $0.060/h), but the public /v2/plans API returns hourly_cost = monthly/730 (e.g. vc2-4c-8gb 0.055). The card uses monthly/672 (the documented billing rule); if Vultr actually bills the API rate, part-time costs are ~8% lower.
Minimum billing unit is 1 hour (every started hour billed). Stopped instances and stopped bare metal bill in full until destroyed.
GPU instances bill on 730 h (actual hours) since 2024-10-01; VX1 bills actual hours with no 672 h cap.

Egress: 2 TB free per account per month plus each instance's allowance accrued hourly (monthly allowance/672 per hour), pooled; overage $0.01/GB; inbound free. egress_free_gib here = 2,048 account + 4,096 of a vc2-4c-8gb (per-instance, prorated) - not an account constant.
Snapshots $0.05/GB-month on compressed size, usable in any region; deploy new instances from a snapshot to clone (fs only, no memory). No snapshots for bare metal.
One public IPv4 per instance is included; Reserved IPs cost $3/month; additional instance IPv4 price not captured.
Pricing may vary by location (e.g. Sao Paulo is 1.5x on many plans in the API location_cost field).
Nested virtualization: documented for VX1 ('support for virtualization') and inherent on bare metal; not documented for vc2/vhp/vhf/voc (null).
Vultr Firewall filters inbound only (egress filtering must be done in the guest).
No published commitment/reserved discounts; free-tier plan vc2-1c-0.5gb-free (1 vCPU/0.5 GB, $0) exists in SEA/FRA/MIA per API; promo-code credits not captured.
Default account instance limit not published; 50 concurrent instances likely needs a limit increase.
vultr.com is Cloudflare-protected; website figures come from the Wayback snapshot of 2026-09-26 and docs.vultr.com; plan specs from the unauthenticated API on 2026-09-28.

Boot / provisioning time is not published for vc2, vhp, vhf, voc or VX1 ("ready for use in seconds" is the only VX1 claim), so boot_overhead_s stays null; with 1-hour minimum billing, boot time sits inside the first billed hour anyway. A new instance also needs OS setup (DIY VM, no sandbox API).
Automatic backups add 20% to the instance price; DDoS protection $10/mo per instance; Reserved IPs $3/mo ($0.004/h); promo-code credits expire and require a linked card/PayPal (one promo per user).

Free Tier Program: application-only, randomized/weighted admission, limited regions; API plan vc2-1c-0.5gb-free (1 vCPU / 0.5 GB / 10 GB, $0) is deployable in sea/fra/mia. Not modelled as free credit.

fleet.verification: Consistent usage and positive billing history; request confirms profile, organization size and use case.
fleet.notes: Console Billing > Limits shows maximum instance count and total instance cost. Request Custom Limit Adjustment or support ticket; initial numeric caps, GPU-specific allowance and turnaround are not published in reviewed guidance.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: However, Automatic Backups run automatically but you must take a snapshot manually.
snapshot_auto.note: Plain VPS: stopping an instance does not checkpoint it (disk simply persists; no idle stop). Automatic Backups are scheduled (paid add-on), disk/file system only, and do not include attached Block Storage - that is not snapshot_auto.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of an instance's state, including its entire file system and disk contents.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Console / API (POST /v2/snapshots) / vultr-cli; disk only, no memory; can take up to 30 min. New instances can be deployed from a snapshot in any region ('you can provision a new instance in New York using the same snapshot image'). $0.05/GB-month compressed. Not available on Bare Metal. Block Storage has its own volume snapshots.

harness_api.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
harness_api.note: Generic IaaS; no first-party API drives a coding agent/harness inside the instance.

egress_allowlist.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_allowlist.note: Firewall groups are inbound-only; outbound filtering must be done in the guest (iptables/ufw). VPC gives private networking but no egress policy.

egress_http_rules.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side outbound filtering of any kind for Cloud Compute.

ingress_rules.quote: Vultr Firewall groups allow you to create rules that filter incoming network traffic to an instance. Firewall rules define the network ports and services to control, filter, and secure network connections to the instance.
ingress_rules.note: Firewall groups (IP/CIDR + protocol/port rules, attach to many instances), plus VPC private networking. Public IPv4 per instance.

guest_firewall.quote: if the Vultr Firewall allows HTTPS traffic but the instance’s internal firewall blocks HTTPS, the traffic will still be blocked, because the instance-level firewall does not permit it.
guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VM with root; Vultr docs include iptables/ufw/firewalld guides.

secret_proxy.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
secret_proxy.note: Plain VPS; no first-party proxy that injects credentials for outbound HTTP calls. Secrets are only whatever the customer places in env vars/user-data/files inside the VM.

volume_attach.quote: Yes, you can attach up to 16 Vultr Block Storage volumes to the same Vultr Cloud Compute instance.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage (same location as instance), detach/move between instances; not covered by Automatic Backups.

volume_shared.quote: Yes, you can attach multiple Vultr Cloud Compute instances to a single Vultr File System volume provided the instance and the volume are in the same Vultr location.
volume_shared.note: Vultr File System (VFS), virtiofs, read-write, same location only; Linux and Windows instances simultaneously. Block Storage itself is single-attach ('you can only attach a Vultr Block Storage volume to one Vultr Cloud Compute instance at a time').

pause_resume.quote: Explains Vultrs billing policy for instances that are stopped but not destroyed, confirming charges continue while resources remain allocated.
pause_resume.note: Cloud Compute only has stop/start/reboot, not a distinct pause action, and stopping does not reduce billing (full charges continue until the instance is destroyed), so there is no pause/resume with paused or reduced billing.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of an instance's state, including its entire file system and disk contents.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Vultr snapshots and new-instance-from-snapshot cover disk/filesystem only; there is no memory-state snapshot/fork (no hibernate-to-clone of a live process tree) documented anywhere in the compute product.

desktop.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
desktop.note: Vultr Cloud Compute is a bare KVM VPS/IaaS product; it ships no managed graphical desktop (VNC/RDP/stream) service. Any RDP/GUI access on a Windows instance is the customer's own OS-level setup, not a provider feature. Outside the product's scope.

browser.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
browser.note: Generic IaaS VM product; no managed/preinstalled browser is offered or documented. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
computer_use.note: No screenshot/click-driving API exists for a plain VPS; this capability is outside what the product is.

wake_on_request.quote: Explains Vultrs billing policy for instances that are stopped but not destroyed, confirming charges continue while resources remain allocated.
wake_on_request.note: Cloud Compute instances are always-on VMs with manual start/stop; there is no documented mechanism for a stopped instance to wake automatically when a request arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Explains Vultrs billing policy for instances that are stopped but not destroyed, confirming charges continue while resources remain allocated.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle-detection/auto-stop feature is documented for Cloud Compute; instances run and bill continuously until the customer manually stops or destroys them.

inbound_https.quote: One public IPv4 address is included with every Vultr Cloud Compute instance.
inbound_https.note: Vultr gives a raw public IPv4 (and raw TCP ingress) per instance; there is no provider-managed HTTPS URL/endpoint to reach a port - the customer must bring their own domain, reverse proxy and TLS certificate inside the guest.

agent_harnesses.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
agent_harnesses.note: Vultr's One-Click Apps/Marketplace catalog is standard web/app stacks (CMS, databases, dev tools); no Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode-style coding-agent templates are offered.

macos.note: Every Cloud Compute and Bare Metal plan in the public plans/plans-metal API runs on Intel or AMD x86 hardware; no Apple silicon / macOS host is offered anywhere in Vultr's catalog.

arm64.note: All 151 plans returned by /v2/plans list cpu_vendor as Intel or AMD only; no ARM/Graviton-style plan type exists in the API.

self_host.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
self_host.note: Vultr is a public multi-tenant cloud provider selling VM/bare-metal capacity in its own data centers; it is not software a customer can run on their own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment model; Vultr only sells capacity inside its own regions/data centers.

open_source.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers. 100% KVM Virtualization
open_source.note: Vultr's compute platform, control panel and orchestration stack are closed-source proprietary cloud software; no OSI-licensed core product exists.
